jobs.title: Research Assistant Professor - Computational Biology or Systems Immunology
jobs.description:
CAREERS AT OKLAHOMA MEDICAL RESEARCH FOUNDATION

Have big ideas, passion, and a desire to grow? Join us and make a difference.

For multiple consecutive years, Foundation employees have voted OMRF among “Oklahoma’s Top Workplaces.”

Our mission: "...so that more may live longer, healthier lives." Learn more .
Research Assistant Professor - Computational Biology or Systems Immunology

Position Overview and Responsibilities
The James/Guthridge Lab (james.omrf.org ; guthridge.omrf.org ) is hiring a Research Assistant Professor (transitional faculty member) to assist with analysis of large, complex, multi-modal datasets from clinical trials and clinical research protocols. The successful candidate will have training and expertise in computational biology, systems immunology, bioinformatics, biostatistics, machine learning, or related quantitative disciplines to add to one of the nation's leading multidisciplinary autoimmune disease research programs, OMRF Arthritis & Clinical Immunology .

This position offers an exceptional opportunity to become part of a highly collaborative team of physician-scientists, immunologists, computational biologists, geneticists, epidemiologists, and data scientists dedicated to understanding the mechanisms underlying autoimmune diseases and developing strategies to predict, prevent, and treat them.

The successful candidate will leverage large, deeply phenotyped, multi-modal datasets generated from patients with autoimmune diseases and individuals at risk for developing autoimmunity. Available data include high-dimensional molecular, cellular, genetic, genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, clinical, imaging, and longitudinal biospecimen datasets derived from peripheral blood and disease-relevant tissues. These resources provide outstanding opportunities for integrative analyses, biomarker discovery, mechanistic investigation, disease prediction, and precision medicine.

This is a transitional position for scientists who have completed a graduate degree and an exemplary postdoctoral experience who have been evaluated as being likely to develop high-caliber independent or collaborative projects and to attract extramural grant support. Successful candidates are characterized by considerable experience, highly distinctive competence, and a demonstrated ability to perform both independently and as a critical member of a large multi-disciplinary productive team.
Minimum Qualifications
• Ph.D. in a biological science, chemistry, physics or other relevant area such as statistics, biostatistics, applied mathematics, epidemiology, and/or M.D., or equivalent and typically two or more years of exemplary postdoctoral experience.
• Must be a team-player with good organizational and communication skills.
• Must be able to work independently, as well as highly attentive to detail, and dependable.
• Must be interested in contributing to the preparation and development of federal and foundation grant applications.

Preferred Qualifications
• The ability to perform data analysis and visualization using appropriate analytic software programs or through programming in R, Python or other languages.
• Human Immune response in heath and disease experience or clinical trials experience strongly preferred.
• At least 5 publications, including publications in high-impact journals.
• Experience writing parts of successful grant applications.

OMRF Overview
Founded in 1946, the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation (OMRF) is among the nation’s oldest, most respected independent, nonprofit biomedical research institutes. OMRF is dedicated to understanding and developing more effective treatments for human diseases, focusing on critical research areas such as Alzheimer’s disease, cancer, lupus, multiple sclerosis, and…

jobs.title: Scientific Programmer I - Algorithm Integration
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The Scientific Programmer I - Algorithm Integration supports the integration, testing, and operational readiness of scientific algorithms and software products in a remote work environment. This role documents algorithm workflows, establishes testing processes, validates outputs, troubleshoots issues, and ensures reliable delivery of production-ready solutions.

Success in this role is demonstrated through accurate algorithm implementation, effective collaboration with Science Teams and stakeholders, and the successful transition of validated software into operational environments.

What You Will Do in This Role

The Scientific Programmer II - Algorithm Integration supports the operationalization of scientific algorithms by documenting requirements, integrating and validating code, establishing testing processes, ensuring output accuracy, and collaborating with scientific and technical stakeholders to deliver reliable production-ready solutions.
• Analyze and document algorithm inputs, outputs, workflows, and production rules across operational units, identifying variations in requirements and implementation approaches.
• Define and maintain operational execution procedures, including run triggers, intermediate data exchanges, processing workflows, and final delivered output products.
• Establish, maintain, and validate project baseline test cases in collaboration with Science Teams to support consistent software verification.
• Evaluate code updates and enhancements against established baselines to identify impacts, maintain functionality, and support regression testing activities.
• Review and analyze regression test results to identify issues, verify fixes, and ensure continued algorithm reliability.
• Coordinate with Science Teams and technical stakeholders to communicate progress, resolve issues, manage dependencies, and track project activities through tools such as Jira.
• Integrate and validate software components in alignment with coding standards, interface requirements, build processes, and project documentation checklists.
• Verify output products for accuracy, quality, format compliance, logging requirements, and adherence to operational standards.
• Troubleshoot, optimize, and debug code while supporting updates to input/output file formats and data processing workflows.
• Develop and maintain technical documentation, including production rules, delivery documentation, operational procedures, and user guidance materials.
• Demonstrate delivered software capabilities and production workflows while providing technical support during transition to operational environments.
• Develop and execute test cases to evaluate impacts from upstream data changes and support downstream algorithm enhancements.

What You Will Bring
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
• 2-4 years of experience in system integration, software deployment, or IT operations.
• Hands-on experience with one or more of the following programming languages: FORTRAN, C, or C++, supporting application development, integration, maintenance, or performance-focused initiatives.
• Working knowledge of Python for application support, scripting, or automation.
• Strong understanding of configuration management, APIs, system interfaces, and data flow between interconnected systems.
• Experience with container technologies, preferably Docker, and container orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes.
• Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot, analyze, and resolve complex software integration issues.
• Strong documentation, communication, and coordination skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical teams.

Work authorization/security clearance requirements
• Ability to obtain a security clearance.

Work Environment
• This work is normally completed in a remote environment.

Physical Demands
• Prolonged periods of sitting
